source.valueAuthority: Detailed prose sections plus user confirmation

baseGrid.halfStepPolicy: Use only for optical calibration, compact controls, icon-text alignment, stroke compensation, or constrained component sizes.
rules: Use multiples of 4 for page margins, card gaps, container padding and content spacing.
Avoid 4px as regular vertical spacing; reserve it for the smallest internal relationships.
Do not use odd values for page structure, card layout or primary content spacing.
Use 1px only for strokes and dividers, not layout spacing.

L1.usage: 页面主要内容区、核心业务模块

L2.usage: 一级卡片内的功能分区

L3.usage: 信息分组、列表模块、小型内容区

L4.usage: 局部信息块、轻量嵌套区域

cardRules: Determine card level from information hierarchy, not visual appearance or nesting count alone.

L1 background cards are borderless by default; use background contrast, spacing and radius to create hierarchy. Add a semantic border only when same-color separation, selection or interaction boundaries, or an explicit design source requires it.
Keep horizontal and vertical gaps equal within the same card group by default.
For strong vertical reading rhythm, vertical gap may be one scale step larger than horizontal gap, but remain consistent within the module.
For adjacent cards of different levels, derive spacing from their common parent or higher level; do not add margins from both cards.
Define title-to-content spacing independently; do not enlarge card padding to create it.
Lists, tables and images may locally bleed to an edge, while headings and primary text remain aligned to the content baseline.
Nested card padding should normally be smaller than outer-card padding.
Do not compress card padding below 8px.

requirements: Interactive components in the same visual level, action group, or form row use the same size tier and visible control height.
The parent composition selects the size once and propagates it to Button, Input, Selector, DatePicker and comparable controls.
Do not mix sizes to fill width, fit isolated text, or patch layout problems; wrap or revise layout first.
exceptions: A component contract mandates a distinct embedded size, such as compact table-row actions or pagination controls.
An explicit design instance intentionally separates hierarchy and still preserves baseline, hit-area and visual alignment.

rules: Keep left and right margins equal within one page.
When a fixed sidebar, navbar or centered max-width container exists, measure card spacing from the content-container boundary.
Combine density margins with responsive viewport rules; responsive.json remains authoritative for browser-width transitions.

flexibility: Adjust only to adjacent scale steps based on viewport, density, component type and business context.
Keep the same level, type and scenario consistent.
Dense back-office and dashboards may reduce one step; presentation and marketing pages may increase one step.
When space is insufficient, optimize layout and information structure before reducing padding.
Dialogs, drawers, overlays and table containers follow their component-specific rules first.
